comparator.academicYear: Published indicative 2027–2028 prospectus curriculum for each of the three listed years; later cohorts may change
comparator.sourceNotes: Radboud lists 60 EC of required legal study in each year of the standard pathway. Its separate French–Dutch legal translation specialisation modifies the second year and is not combined here. The third year includes 56 EC of required courses and one 4-EC restricted choice; Philosophy of Law is one permitted choice. The 0-EC first-year tutorial is outside the credited curriculum. The official year pages call the 2027–2028 listing provisional for prospective students and do not promise these exact courses for a Fall 2026 entrant.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Law, Society & Justice precedes all formally dependent 200/300-level law courses; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law. Comparative politics and sociology foundations precede advanced EU politics and social theory, and all course offerings and formal prerequisites are satisfied.

It implements the explicit academic basis “Dutch constitutional, administrative, criminal and private law, including civil procedure and comparative constitutional law” and “Public international law, cross-border legal relations and legal argumentation”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One 24-course law-led response captures the Dutch, EU and international law core with explicitly limited Dutch procedural and civil-law depth. The French–Dutch translation specialisation is not feasible with the current UCR course offer; legal advocacy is already substantively integrated into the first alternative and cannot justify a distinct second curriculum.

notes.text: Radboud offers a three-year Dutch, EU and international law sequence with extensive Dutch private and procedural law and a required legal thesis. UCR combines selected law courses with politics, society and communication, but does not reproduce Radboud’s depth or professional legal qualification pathway.
